## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: author names, affiliations, acknowledgements and explicit mentions of the author's institution go on a separate page; normally two independent reviewers |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Not stated on the guidelines page read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No; reviewers' comments are generally sent to authors unedited unless offensive or confidential, and reviewers see the full set of reports and the decision (guidelines) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Not stated by the journal. SciRev n=1: 3.0 rounds |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Editors state the referees' advice is important but they may reach a different view; rejected submissions receive no correspondence (guidelines) |

> Source: guidelines page via Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20 (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html). Exceptions to double-blind review: papers rejected for quality/relevance without comments, and invited reflections, invited papers and solicited book reviews, which are generally reviewed by the editors. Editor-authored papers go to editors unaffiliated with the author.

## Format

Source for this section: guidelines page via Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20 (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html); policies may have changed since.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Submitted article (unsolicited); contribution to symposium, critical notice, and current-directions essay (all solicited by the editors); reply to critical notice. The page says the journal does not publish discussion notes or unsolicited reviews |
| **Word limit** | 10,000 words including notes and references; the word count must be embedded in the document or the submission is returned |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Authors may make a case for exceeding the limit on submission; the journal says it does not expect to allow exceptions regularly. A revised paper should grow by no more than about 10% |
| **Abstract limit** | Abstract required; no word limit stated on the page. Up to seven keywords |
| **Reference limit** | No numeric limit; any consistent style accepted at submission; keep to essential items and minimise substantive footnotes |
| **Supplementary material** | Figures, supporting information and appendices as separate files; main text in Word (preferred) or LaTeX with a PDF |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated; figures and tables should have legends |

### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 0268-1064 and 1468-0017, journal articles dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 304 articles, of which 274 (90%) carry a deposited abstract, retrieved 2026-11-23. Keywords were matched locally in title plus abstract, shares are of the 274 with abstracts, and all counts are lower bounds. OpenAlex `works` queries were not available (daily budget exhausted), so Crossref was used.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Philosophical argument is the main mode: "argu*" in 168 of 274 abstracts (61.3%), "philosoph*" 63 (23.0%). Empirical work is present but secondary: "empirical" 33 (12.0%), "experiment*" 18 (6.6%), "participants" 10 (3.6%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Few method terms of the social-science kind: "survey/questionnaire" 5 (1.8%), "qualitative" 2 (0.7%), "interview" 0; modelling terms are more common ("computational/Bayes/formal model" 17, 6.2%) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Aims and scope name linguistics, philosophy, psychology, artificial intelligence, cognitive anthropology and cognitive archaeology (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/productinformation.html, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-03). Counts: "psycholog*" 49 (17.9%), "linguistic" 42 (15.3%), "semantic*" 41 (15.0%), "cognitive scien*" 14 (5.1%), neuro-terms 20 (7.3%), AI/language-model terms 11 (4.0%) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the aims page says the journal brings together mind and language research in a genuinely interdisciplinary way and publishes original articles, forums, survey articles and reviews (same URL). Recent Crossref titles (November 2026) include "How LLMs might think" (DOI 10.1111/mila.70049), "Teleosemantics for neural word embeddings" (10.1111/mila.70037), "Agency, AI, and acting for a purpose of the agent" (10.1111/mila.70065), "Permissible presupposition" (10.1111/mila.70038) and "The big-small problem in infant number cognition" (10.1111/mila.70063). The previous pass's description of Early View items came from search snippets and is replaced by these Crossref records.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic philosophical argument about mind, language and representation; experimental or empirical cognitive-science and psycholinguistics studies; computational/Bayesian modelling; philosophy-of-AI papers; symposium, critical-notice and reply formats (by invitation).

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Scope statement: the guidelines page says the journal "is committed to equality and diversity and welcomes submissions from all groups" in its areas (guidelines, Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20); no political or epistemological stance is stated on the pages read.
- Terms in titles/abstracts of 274 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): "representation" 47 (17.2%), predictive processing or Bayes 7 (2.6%), teleosemantic or naturalis* 8 (2.9%), phenomenolog* 10 (3.6%), Gricean/relevance theory/Sperber 4 (1.5%), Frege 4 (1.5%), Wittgenstein or Kripke 3 (1.1%), Fodor or Chomsky 3 (1.1%), Kant 0, feminis*/social justice/oppress*/stereotyp* 5 (1.8%).
- Most-cited list on the journal homepage (Crossref citations in the last three years, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-19, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/14680017): Sperber et al. "Epistemic Vigilance" (2010), Hohwy "New directions in predictive processing" (2020), Sperber and Wilson "Pragmatics, Modularity and Mind-reading" (2002), Martin "The Transparency of Experience" (2002).
- Editorial Advisory Board lists, among others, N. Chomsky, N. Block, T. Burge, D. Sperber and R. Stalnaker (board page, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-03).
- Reading of the counts: the published pattern is analytic, naturalistic philosophy of mind and language in dialogue with cognitive science and linguistics; social-political frameworks are rare. This describes what is published, not editors' politics.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: the guidelines require that all submissions be intelligible to an interdisciplinary audience (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html, Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20); the aims page defines scope as work on mind and language across linguistics, philosophy, psychology, AI, cognitive anthropology and cognitive archaeology (productinformation page, snapshot 2025-06-03).
- Article types: unsolicited submitted articles of up to 10,000 words including notes and references; critical notices, symposium contributions and current-directions essays are solicited; discussion notes and unsolicited reviews are not published (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html).
- Concision is a stated criterion: the guidelines say papers seen as unnecessarily long are less likely to be accepted, and that editors may ask for cuts to articles of any length (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html).
- Crossref titles show the solicited formats in use: of 304 articles 2021-2026, titles containing reply/response number 11 and commentary/comment-on titles 6 (own count, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: the guidelines say submissions may be rejected without comments if the editors judge the paper does not meet quality and/or relevance requirements; no rejection rate is published.

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule (this pass's own convention, not the journal's): hits divided by the 274 articles with abstracts, 2021-2026; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need a cited editorial statement and none was found. Source: Crossref titles/abstracts for ISSN 0268-1064, retrieved 2026-11-23; counts are lower bounds.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Philosophical argument / conceptual analysis | 3 | "argu*" 168 articles (61.3%), "philosoph*" 63 (23.0%); capped at 3 by rule though clearly the dominant mode; the phrase "conceptual analysis" appears 0 times |
| Empirical studies (general) | 3 | "empirical" 33 articles (12.0%) |
| Behavioural experiments | 3 | "experiment*" 18 articles (6.6%) |
| Neuroscience / neuroimaging | 3 | 20 articles (7.3%) matching "neuro*, fMRI, EEG"; the stem also matches neural-network papers, so this overstates imaging work |
| Computational / Bayesian / formal modelling | 3 | 17 articles (6.2%) |
| Survey / questionnaire | 2 | 5 articles (1.8%) |
| Case study | 2 | 3 articles (1.1%); in philosophy abstracts this often means an example case, not a method |
| Corpus / eye-tracking / reaction-time methods | 1 | 2 articles (0.7%) |
| Qualitative methods | 1 | 2 articles (0.7%) |
| Interviews | 0 | 0 articles in 274 |

### Voice & Style

- Title and keywords: a short informative title without abbreviations, abstract, up to seven keywords; references in any consistent style at submission (guidelines, Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20).
- Style guidance stated: submissions intelligible to an interdisciplinary audience; minimise substantive footnotes; avoid long parenthetical reference lists (same page).
- Authorship pattern: 211 of 274 articles with author data (77%) have a single author (Crossref, own count, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- First-person use in abstracts (274 abstracts, Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): "I" appears in 149 (54%), "we" in 102 (37%), any of I/my/we/our in 221 (81%); "this paper/article/essay" in 95 (35%). Examples: "In this paper, I tackle..." (DOI 10.1111/mila.70068); "I argue" (10.1111/mila.70038).
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1111/mila.70063 opens with a phenomenon ("When subitizing, infants precisely discriminate..."); 10.1111/mila.70038 opens with a question; 10.1111/mila.70065 opens with a general claim about animal agency; 10.1111/mila.70069 describes what "This paper develops"; 10.1111/mila.70047 and 10.1111/mila.70060 open by naming the book under discussion (symposium format); 10.1111/mila.70066 is a reply written in the first person ("my 2024 book").

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

- Review model: double-blind, normally two reviewers (guidelines, Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20). The homepage notes that anonymous reviewing was formerly offered and is now a requirement of submission (homepage, snapshot 2025-06-19).
- Editorial board (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/editorialboard.html, Wayback snapshot 2025-06-03): 43 named people (Executive Editor, 12 Editors, 7 Consulting Editors, 23 Advisory Board members). All 13 Executive Editor and Editors list a UK institution (York 3, UCL 4, Warwick 2, Birmingham, Birkbeck, Reading, Oxford 1 each); the 7 Consulting Editors list US (5) and Australian (2) institutions. Disciplines are not labelled on the page.
- Executive Editor as listed: Gregory Currie, University of York (same page).
- Referee turnaround asked by the journal: eight weeks (guidelines).
- OpenAlex-derived topic mix of the journal's output (spine, 2026-07-13): Philosophy and Theoretical Science 318, Epistemology/Ethics/Metaphysics 229, Syntax/Semantics/Linguistic Variation 224, Child and Animal Learning Development 211.
- APA Journal Survey (self-reported by submitters): average 1.8 reviewers per submission, 63.9% of submissions received comments, 72 initial verdicts (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/683, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- One first-hand submitter comment in the APA survey (a 2020 submission, rejected, 2 reviewers, https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/683, retrieved 2026-11-23): the two sets of reviewer comments differed in quality, one perceptive and helpful, the other meandering and unclear; n=1, an anecdote.
- Reviewer behaviour itself (tone, expectations) is not observable from public pages; the one SciRev review rates comment difficulty 2.0/5.0 (easy) and report quality 3.0/5.0 (n=1).

### Practical Concerns

- Ethics and integrity: the manuscript must include details of IRB approvals, ethical treatment of human and animal participants and informed consent as appropriate; conflicts of interest declared on submission; COPE core practices followed; iThenticate overlap checking (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html, Wayback snapshot 2022-02-20).
- Data: the journal encourages data sharing and asks for a data availability statement (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html).
- Authorship and identifiers: all authors must have contributed substantially and agreed to the final version; ORCID is required (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html).
- Submission: via ScholarOne (mc.manuscriptcentral.com/mila); free-format submission accepted; the journal does not charge submission fees; a manuscript in poor English may be returned (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680017/homepage/forauthors.html).
- Preprints: allowed at any time, link the final article afterwards (same page).
- OA and charges: hybrid with OnlineOpen; APC figure unverified (see Open Access table).
- AI: disclosure per Wiley policy (URL in the AI Policy table).
- Anonymisation: all identifying information, including acknowledgements, goes on a separate page (same page).
- Independent-scholar rules and fee waivers: not stated on the pages read.

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A non-anonymised manuscript: double-blind review, with author details and acknowledgements on a separate page (Peer Review table).
- A submission over 10,000 words including notes and references, without a case made for exceeding it; the word count must be embedded or the paper is returned (Format table).
- Discussion notes and unsolicited reviews: the journal states it does not publish them (Format table).
- Undisclosed generative-AI use beyond minor editing (AI Policy table).

### Soft Tax

- Concision: the guidelines say unnecessarily long papers are less likely to be accepted, and a revision should grow by no more than about 10% (Format table, Framing Requirements).
- Timeline risk: sources disagree (Wiley homepage 19 days to first decision; APA self-reports 5 months average; SciRev n=1 12.2 months to first round and 17.1 months in total), so no reliable estimate exists (Review Cycle Time).
- Rejection share: 53 of 72 first verdicts in the self-reported APA survey were rejections (73.6%); the sample is self-selected (Metrics table).

### Best Suited For

- Single-author argumentative papers on mind, language and representation: "argu*" in 61.3% of abstracts and 77% of articles single-authored (Orientation, Voice & Style).
- Philosophy papers that engage cognitive science or linguistics: "empirical" in 12.0%, "experiment*" in 6.6% and "semantic*" in 15.0% of abstracts (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work on AI and language models as a philosophy-of-mind topic: 11 articles (4.0%) including several 2026 titles (Orientation).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers that need interviews or qualitative field methods: 0 interview and 2 qualitative articles in 274 (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Social-political or identity-focused work as the main topic: race 1, gender 0, politics 1 article (Sensitive Topics); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a predictable decision time: published and self-reported figures conflict (Review Cycle Time).
